policy: Do not perform broad directory moves while governance contracts, examples, and generated-output gates depend on current paths. Strengthen directory boundaries with machine checks first, then migrate one example family at a time after P10 convergence if evidence supports it.

topLevelDirectoryBoundaries.policy: Every tracked top-level directory must have an explicit responsibility, category, and validation gate. New tracked top-level directories are not allowed until this manifest and project-layout-governance-check are updated in the same change.

ignoredArtifactBoundary.policy: Runtime state, generated documentation, benchmark transients, built binaries, and coverage artifacts must stay ignored and untracked. Root aiflow.yaml is the committed workflow contract; .aiflow/ is only local run evidence and temporary state.

artifacts.reason: Local aiflow run evidence and temporary execution state must not be committed.
Local harness execution state must stay outside repository history.
Temporary Go cache, GOTMPDIR, generated project smoke output, and sandbox state must be disposable.
Local agent state is machine-specific and must not affect project layout.
Local planning artifacts are never committed for this repository.
The compiled CLI binary belongs to local builds and release artifacts, not source control.
Coverage output is regenerated by gates and must not be reviewed as source.
Current benchmark output is local run state; committed benchmark evidence lives in tracked baseline and reference files.
Regression reports are regenerated by benchmark gates and should not be mixed with source changes.
Benchmark summaries are local evidence snapshots unless promoted into reference docs.
Generated top-level docs are local render output; curated docs live under allow-listed documentation subdirectories.

docsTaxonomyBoundaries.policy: Every tracked docs subdirectory must belong to exactly one documentation taxonomy family. Generated top-level docs remain ignored, docs/superpowers remains local-only, and new tracked docs subdirectories require this manifest plus project-layout-governance-check updates.

examplesGroupingPlan.migrationPolicy: Keep current examples/* paths stable until a future task migrates one family at a time and updates all gates in the same commit.

readinessContract.policy: Every current example must declare its runnable kind, command, verification command, dependency mode, copyable module state, smoke gate, README source, and rollback note before any future physical grouping is allowed.

Keep the previous reusable middleware catalog until generated-service import and package tests pass.
Keep the source framework path active until every migration case, gate command, and caveat evidence passes.
Keep the previous model generator profile until GORM repository checklist and dependency boundary evidence pass.
Keep the previous model generator profile until Mongo repository checklist and dependency boundary evidence pass.

physicalMigrationAdmission.policy: Examples may move only after one planned family proves copyable modules, smoke commands, docs links, Makefile targets, scripts, and rollback notes can be updated in a single dedicated migration commit.
requiredSignals: one examples family is selected before any path move starts
target family has a dedicated task id and rollback owner
pre-move gates pass with the current examples/* paths
post-move gates pass with the new grouped path
examples/README.md commands and matrix are updated
each moved go.mod module path and local replace directive is updated
bin/scripts and Makefile references to moved paths are updated
docs links and reference evidence point to the new paths
rollback note explains how to restore the old path without losing user guidance

blockers: server examples expose user-facing curl paths that still reference flat examples/* commands
middleware smoke coverage is shared with p1-growth-check and must move as a single explicit family
familyAssessments.rollbackRequirement: Restore the previous flat examples paths and route users through examples/README.md until HTTP smoke and copyable checks pass again.

blockers: RPC examples are tied to boundary evidence and generated IDL paths that must stay explainable
copyable module paths need a dedicated before-and-after replay for resolver and streaming examples
familyAssessments.rollbackRequirement: Restore the previous RPC example paths and keep the old command matrix documented until resolver, stream, and copyable evidence pass.

blockers: production examples span cloud-native assets, reference app smoke, and multi-service ports
Docker-backed and static fallback evidence must stay readable during any path move
familyAssessments.rollbackRequirement: Restore the previous production example paths and keep deployment notes pointing to the flat layout until live and fallback checks pass.

blockers: governance examples are referenced by adoption, plugin, migration, and resilience reports
moving them requires synchronized evidence updates across multiple docs/reference contracts
familyAssessments.rollbackRequirement: Restore the previous governance example paths and keep evidence manifests on the old paths until all governance gates pass.

blockers: data examples cover several dependency modes and generated-project dependency boundaries
the family is too broad to move before cache, model, MQ, and observability path references are isolated
familyAssessments.rollbackRequirement: Restore the previous data example paths and keep model, cache, MQ, and discovery instructions on the flat layout until gates pass.
